cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Must describe all-or-nothing execution or rollback on failure.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for partial description of the all-or-nothing concept.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 1) Atomicity: all-or-nothing / commit all ops or rollback.
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Atomicity: a transaction is all-or-nothing — either every operation commits, or on failure the system rolls back so it looks like the transaction never happened.

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Must describe preservation of integrity constraints or valid state transitions.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for mentioning valid state or integrity constraints alone.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 2) Consistency: preserves integrity constraints / valid state to valid state.
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Consistency: a committed transaction takes the database from one valid state to another, preserving integrity constraints (keys, checks, business rules).

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Must describe non-interference of concurrent transactions or serializability.
acceptable_variants: transactions do not see intermediate states
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for mentioning concurrent transactions do not interfere.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 3) Isolation: concurrent transactions do not see each other's uncommitted/intermediate effects (serializable idea OK).
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Isolation: concurrent transactions do not interfere; the effect is as if transactions ran one after another (serializable, or at least their intermediate states are hidden per the isolation level).

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Must describe persistence of committed data against failure.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for mentioning data survives crashes or is stored permanently.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 4) Durability: committed data survives failure / persisted to stable storage.
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Durability: once a transaction commits, its effects survive crashes/power loss (typically via logging / stable storage).
